facts.text: If I could own just one AI memory stock for the next five years, my choice would be SK Hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY).
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Now, for the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
It's a key player in the $1.8 trillion space race, and with the stock recently sitting 20% off its highs, the window to get in early is closing fast.
Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) has become a major beneficiary of rising demand for memory chips, which has fueled record revenue and earnings growth over the last year.
What investors may not fully understand is that Micron isn't the only company poised to capitalize on artificial intelligence's insatiable appetite for memory.
These processors wouldn't be nearly as effective without high bandwidth memory (HBM).
The companies designing next-generation AI accelerators need memory suppliers capable of meeting increasingly demanding technical requirements.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
